claims.claim: No wealth tax and no capital gains tax

sources.name: PwC: Mauritius, other taxes
sources.says: Last reviewed 15 June 2026. "There are no net wealth/worth taxes in Mauritius." "There are no inheritance, estate, or gift taxes in Mauritius." Registration duty on inherited property is not covered.

sources.name: PwC: Mauritius, income determination
sources.says: Last reviewed 15 June 2026. "There is no tax on capital gains in Mauritius"; "Capital gains received by a resident or non-resident from outside Mauritius are not taxable." "Investment income derived from outside Mauritius is taxable in a resident recipient's hands" when received in or handled from Mauritius, and a foreign tax credit is generally available against the Mauritius tax on it.

claims.claim: Residents (183+ days) pay tax on foreign income only when it is received in Mauritius, so dividends left in the US are untaxed

sources.name: PwC: Mauritius, taxes on personal income
sources.says: Last reviewed 15 June 2026. Residents are taxed on "worldwide income from all sources", but foreign-source income only when received in Mauritius. From 1 July 2025: first MUR 500,000 at 0%, next 500,000 at 10%, remainder at 20%. Fair Share Contribution "at the rate of 15% of their leviable income in excess of MUR 12 million", for the income year from 1 July 2025 and the two following.

sources.name: PwC: Mauritius, residence
sources.says: Last reviewed 15 June 2026. Resident if domiciled in Mauritius (unless the permanent place of abode is outside), or present 270 days or more over the income year and the two before, or "at least 183 days in that income year".

claims.claim: US estate tax applies only above the $15M exemption (2026)

sources.name: IRS: What's new, estate and gift tax
sources.says: The table "Basic exclusion amount for year of death" has the row 2026: $15,000,000 (2025: $13,990,000). The page says the Working Families Tax Cuts, Public Law 119-21, signed July 4, 2025, "amends § 2010(c)(3) by increasing the basic exclusion amount to $15,000,000 for calendar year 2026". Page last reviewed or updated 03-Nov-2026.

sources.name: IRS: Estate tax
sources.says: A return is required when the gross estate, plus adjusted taxable gifts and specific exemption, is more than the filing threshold for the year of death; the table gives 2026: $15,000,000. Page last reviewed or updated 23-Oct-2026.

sources.name: IRS news release IR-2025-103: tax inflation adjustments for tax year 2026
sources.says: "Estates of decedents who die during 2026 have a basic exclusion amount of $15,000,000", up from $13,990,000 for 2025; the release (October 9, 2025) cites Revenue Procedure 2025-32 and is marked as an archival document.

sources.name: IRS: Some nonresidents with U.S. assets must file estate tax returns
sources.says: "U.S. citizens are subject to U.S. estate taxation with respect to their worldwide assets"; Form 706 is required when worldwide assets plus adjusted taxable gifts exceed the basic exclusion amount in effect on the date of death. By contrast a nonresident who is not a citizen files when US-situated assets exceed $60,000. Page last reviewed or updated 27-Jun-2026.
